categories.main_business_segments: Regency Centers is a fully integrated real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns, operates, develops, and redevelops neighborhood and community shopping centers. The company's primary business segment is retail real estate, consisting of acquiring, developing, owning, and operating income-producing shopping centers predominantly anchored by market-leading grocery stores and located in suburban trade areas with compelling demographics across the United States.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company employs standard real estate development, acquisition, and property management methodologies. Core operational methods include leasing management, tenant relationship management, property maintenance and operations, real estate tax and insurance management, and capital deployment strategies. The company utilizes data analytics for market analysis, demographic assessment, and tenant performance monitoring to optimize portfolio performance and identify development opportunities.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers are retail tenants including necessity, service, convenience, and value-based retailers. Key tenant categories include grocery stores (Publix, Albertsons, Kroger, Whole Foods), discount retailers (TJX Companies, Ross Dress for Less), pharmacies (CVS, Walgreens), fitness centers (L.A. Fitness), and local service providers. End markets served are suburban communities across the United States with above-average household incomes and population densities.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in the United States with significant geographic concentration in California (23.4% of annualized base rent), Florida (19.3%), and other major metropolitan areas. As of December 31, 2023, the portfolio spans 24 states with major presence in California, Florida, Texas, Connecticut, New York, Georgia, Colorado, North Carolina, and Washington. The company maintains 24 market offices nationwide with corporate headquarters in Jacksonville, Florida.
categories.supply_chain_position: Regency operates at the downstream end of the real estate supply chain as a property owner and operator. The company directly owns and manages shopping center properties, leasing space to retail tenants and service providers. The company also holds interests in unconsolidated real estate partnerships and joint ventures, positioning it as both a direct operator and a capital partner in real estate investments.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include: (1) owning high-quality neighborhood and community shopping centers anchored by market-leading grocers in desirable suburban metro areas; (2) generating same-property NOI growth ranking at or near the top of shopping center peers; (3) maintaining a disciplined development and redevelopment platform; (4) supporting conservative capital structure with strong balance sheet and liquidity; (5) implementing leading ESG practices; and (6) attracting and retaining exceptional diverse talent. The company focuses on development and redevelopment projects with estimated pro-rata costs of $468.1 million in process.
categories.revenue_model: Regency generates revenue primarily through leasing space in shopping centers. Revenue sources include: (1) base rent from tenant leases (approximately $897.5 million in 2023); (2) recoveries from tenants for operating, maintenance, insurance, and real estate tax expenses ($311.8 million); (3) percentage rent based on tenant sales ($13.0 million); (4) other lease income including termination fees ($20.7 million); and (5) management, transaction, and other fees ($27.0 million). The company also recognizes straight-line rent and above/below market rent amortization.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Regency is among the largest owners of shopping centers in the USA based on revenues, number of properties, GLA, and market capitalization. The company competes with other major REITs, private real estate companies, and grocery store chains that own shopping centers. Competitive advantages include: market locations with compelling demographics, high-quality shopping centers, strong tenant relationships, experienced leadership team, and proven development and acquisition capabilities. The company is an S&P 500 Index member since 2017.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2023, Regency owned full or partial interests in 482 properties encompassing 56.8 million square feet of GLA (pro-rata share of 48.6 million SF). The company reported net income attributable to common shareholders of $359.5 million in 2023 compared to $482.9 million in 2022. Market capitalization was approximately $10.5 billion as of the last business day of the second quarter 2023. The company completed the acquisition of Urstadt Biddle Properties in August 2023 for approximately $1.14 billion, adding 74 properties and 5.3 million SF of GLA.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Regency's value proposition centers on providing high-quality, well-maintained neighborhood and community shopping centers in suburban trade areas with compelling demographics and above-average household incomes. Differentiation includes: (1) portfolio anchored by market-leading grocery stores that drive consistent customer traffic; (2) focus on necessity, service, and convenience retailers less vulnerable to e-commerce disruption; (3) strategic locations in desirable suburban markets with strong population demographics; (4) active development and redevelopment platform creating modern, attractive retail environments; (5) disciplined capital allocation and conservative balance sheet; and (6) commitment to ESG practices and community engagement.
